note: The working list. Seeded from this file so a deploy carries it; ticked off on the site. A slug keys each task, so a redeploy neither duplicates one nor un-ticks it.

tasks.title: Ada Jessop's household to 25 Cavendish Crescent South
tasks.detail: Three records under "Cavendish Crescent South" on the unfiled page — Ada Jessop, 60, Head, with Anne Draw and Ellen Annie Bess. #49 is the Jessop house and holds nothing in 1921.

tasks.title: The Mather and Talbot households to 19 Cavendish Crescent South
tasks.detail: Seven people, two Heads on one schedule — Charles Talbot manages the glove fabric department for George Mather and lives in his house. The page splits them into two blocks; send both to 46. #46 is free for 1921 now the Brownswords have moved to 15.

tasks.title: The Dowson household to Felixstowe
tasks.detail: Six records in the group "Felixstowe see 1911 Clumber rd W" — William Enfield Dowson, Helena (Town Councillor and JP), and four servants. To #394.

tasks.title: The Homberger household to The Lindens
tasks.detail: The other six in the same group, headed by Kate A Homberger with no head on the return. To #87, Linden House, on the note "Otto Homberger, Of The Lindens, Clumber Road West".

tasks.title: Move the four Dexter brothers from Overdale to Thorsmore
tasks.detail: They are already filed — eight records at #58, 58 Cavendish Road East (Overdale): the four brothers, Emma Savage the housekeeper and three maids, entries 2656 to 2663. But their schedule header reads Thorsmore, which is #36, 22 and 24 Cavendish Crescent North. So this is a move, not a filing: /reassign?prop=58&year=1921, the Dexter block, send all to 36. Overdale also holds the Dobbs household, which stays.

tasks.title: Settle where the Dobson household belongs
tasks.detail: Eight records: John George Dobson, retired cotton doubler, his family and two servants. 5 Cavendish Crescent North already holds the Henderson household for 1921, so one of the two is wrong. Check the Dobson schedule header.

tasks.title: Settle where the Wright household belongs
tasks.detail: The four who sit after the Dobsons on the same page — Bernard Swanwick Wright, a solicitor of 45, Kathleen Florence Wright, Mary Jovan and Minnie Creswell. A household of their own, not Dobsons.

tasks.title: The Lloyd household to 6 Peveril Drive
tasks.detail: Three records in "PeD1 Peveril Drive": Edward Evans Lloyd, 68, Hannah Stanger Lloyd and Ida Maud Gill. Hannah is already filed at #292 as a widow in 1921, on the same person record — that is what places them.

tasks.title: Set aside the rest of Peveril Drive
tasks.detail: Once the Lloyds are out, the other six 1911 households and the five 1921 ones gave no house name and no number. Nothing more the census can do with them.

tasks.title: Merge Johanne Goodliffe / Johanna Goodcliffe
tasks.detail: One woman born 1837, ten years apart on Peveril Drive. Different surname spellings, so they never sit in the same group. Keep #639, merge in #1271.

tasks.title: Merge Florence / Florance Agnes Taylor
tasks.detail: Both born 1893, a servant on Peveril Drive in 1911 and back on it in 1921. Florence against Florance. Keep #638, merge in #1268.

tasks.title: Merge Catherine Charlotte Slack / Black
tasks.detail: Both born 1892, both housemaids of 19 in the same house. The surname itself is mis-transcribed. Keep #263, merge in #774.

tasks.title: Merge Ernest / Earnest Jardine
tasks.detail: Born 1859 and 1860, the same lace machine builder, one record unfiled and one at 9 Clumber Crescent South. Keep #1315, merge in #2573.

tasks.title: Merge Edna Winifred / Edna Jardine
tasks.detail: His daughter, the same double import. Keep #2387, merge in #2574.

tasks.title: Merge Iris Gwendoline / Iris Jardine
tasks.detail: His other daughter, the same double import. Keep #2391, merge in #2575.

tasks.title: Merge the four Jessop pairs
tasks.detail: Ada, Effie, Florence and Rose — one household at 25 Cavendish Crescent South entered twice from two transcriptions. These four now show on the duplicates page under "one household entered twice". Blanche Gertrude Fagan appears only in the second import, so she is a real person, not a duplicate.

tasks.title: Merge Robert and Mary Mouring / Bouring
tasks.detail: The same double import at 9 Clumber Crescent South, with the surname mangled. And Beatrice Fanny Perkins, who came through the second time as "Beatrice Fanny Beatrice".

tasks.title: Place the rest of the Cavendish Crescent North group
tasks.detail: After the Dexters, the Dobsons and the Wrights there are four households left: William Wing's and William Bradshaw's from 1911, and Thomas Berridge Cox's and Henry Holford's from 1921. Free on the crescent in 1921: 9, 15, 18a and Haddon House.

tasks.title: Which house was Kentmere, Cavendish Crescent North? (William Wing, 1911)
tasks.detail: William Wing's 1911 schedule gives Kentmere, Cavendish Crescent North — so the Wings were on the crescent, not on Peveril Drive as this task used to guess. Kentmere is in the record under no name, nor on OpenStreetMap or Dougal's map. The round runs 4 Peveril Drive, then the Wings, then William Bradshaw, then 3 Cavendish Crescent North — so Kentmere is one of the first two houses on the crescent. 1 Cavendish Crescent North (Carisbrooke House) is empty in 1911 and is the obvious candidate: names on this crescent changed, and 10 was formerly Charnwood. That leaves Bradshaw needing a house too — and every other house before No. 3 is either full in 1911 or not in the record. If the schedule gives a number, that settles it.

tasks.title: Place the Allchurch household
tasks.detail: Nine people — William J Allchurch, 37, his wife Mabel, two small children and five servants including a sick nurse — unfiled under "Felixstowe see 1911 Clumber Rd West". Nothing confirms them at Felixstowe in 1921, so take that label off: Change label on the group, leave it empty, Save. The surname is Allchurch for him and Achurch for the rest and will need reconciling.

tasks.title: Check whether Duke William Mount can be set aside
tasks.detail: 14 records with the shape of the Peveril Drive groups. SR1 South Rd was listed here too, but part of it turns out to be a double import of 3 South Road — see that task instead.

tasks.title: Work the rest of the unresolved queue down
tasks.detail: Whatever is left after the named groups above. The page gathers them by address, so most of it is a handful of decisions rather than a record at a time.

tasks.title: 39 Newcastle Drive, 1921 — 27 people under 22 surnames
tasks.detail: The worst on the list. Almost certainly several households filed against one address.

tasks.title: 5 Tattershall Drive, 1921 — 26 people under 16 surnames
19 Park Terrace, 1921 — send the Kneebone block to Broxtowe House
tasks.detail: Three schedules under one address: the Clarks at 19, the nine resident doctors at Broxtowe House (#406), and the Carr household. The doctors are the clear one.

tasks.title: 9 Cavendish Crescent North, 1911 — split the three schedules
tasks.detail: Four servants with no head belong to Peveril House; the Weinberg and Smith households do not. 10 and 11 Gleadthorpe hold no 1911 record.

tasks.title: 10 Barrack Lane, 1911 — three households to Barrack Yard
tasks.detail: Twelve of the seventeen were at Barrack Yard (#410). Only the Derrys belong at number 10.

tasks.title: Penrhyn House, 1921 — the Houltons and the Radfords
tasks.detail: Two of the four schedules are placed. Penrhyn House was divided into flats so one or both may genuinely belong, but it is worth looking.

tasks.title: Work the remaining flagged property-years
tasks.detail: The page recalculates as you go. Surnames is the stronger signal: a real household is rarely more than two or three families.

tasks.title: File the Spray household to Greendale, 4 Huntingdon Drive
tasks.detail: Settled: Joseph Spray's biography gives Greendale, Huntingdon Drive, and Companies House puts Greendale at number 4. 4 Huntingdon Drive (#146) now carries the name. On /unfiled, send the four records under "Huntingdon Drive (Greendale)" to 146. On /research, record the answer against "Which house on Huntingdon Drive is Greendale?".

tasks.title: Decide whether the far side of Huntingdon Drive should be in the record
tasks.detail: 11 Burnham House, 13 The Magpies, 15 The Coach House, The Hunting Lodge, 17, 18 The Round House and Birchwood are on Dougal's map and none are in the record. HM Land Registry now confirms The Hunting Lodge, The Round House, Birchwood and Swan House on Huntingdon Drive, and The Cottage at 14. Only create them where a census household turns up — that is the rule.

tasks.title: 18 Cavendish Crescent North
tasks.detail: The record holds 18a but not 18, though the descriptions of all four houses in that group name it. Nothing has been found living at it yet.

tasks.title: Confirm the numbers for Haddon House and Hardwicke House
tasks.detail: The walk offers 4 and 2 on Cavendish Crescent North, with a query against both. Neither number is used. Say the word and they go in.

tasks.title: Find where Barrack Yard was
tasks.detail: Three households, twelve people, 1911. Dougal's map notes "Allegedly known as Barrack Yard" at the southern end of the lane, around Pelham Cottages and Reveille.

tasks.title: Settle where Broxtowe House was
tasks.detail: Two households were returned at the name, 230 metres apart in one round. Either two houses carried it or one schedule is out of position.

tasks.title: Which of the two buildings by the tunnel is Gees Lodge
tasks.detail: Penrhyn Cottage is the northern, Tunnel Lodge the southern. Gees Lodge is recorded on the southern as the likelier, which is a judgement and not evidence.

tasks.title: Which house's stables is The Stables, Lenton Road
tasks.detail: 21 Lenton Road's coach house is recorded as separately owned, which is what gives a building its own address. 17 Oakhyrst also has one.

tasks.title: Was Yorke Mews ever its own address
tasks.detail: A mews of Yorke House, 6 North Road. Yorke Cottage is the older name and probably the one to search a census on.

tasks.title: Work down the 171 unmatched names on Dougal's map
tasks.detail: House-shaped names with nothing behind them. Some are subdivisions, some earlier names of houses already held, some genuinely missing. The largest single source of new house names available, and most of it can be done from an armchair.

tasks.title: Find the colour key to Dougal's map
tasks.detail: The colouring appears to encode the architect or the period. Reading it off the scan failed. With the key, the map would name the architect of a great many houses at once.

tasks.title: Add the boarding pupils at Western House School, 1891
tasks.detail: The page totals 5 males and 26 females. Four of the women are in; the rest are the pupils. The school ran from 1874 to 1937 and the record holds two nights of it.

tasks.title: Check nothing else on the Felixstowe 1901 page was missed
tasks.detail: The eleven Dowsons are in, with the servants' birthplaces read off the original. Benjamin Dowson's biography could take more — he was a Nottingham solicitor with a practice from 1870.

tasks.title: Re-upload the six portraits lost before Cloudinary
tasks.detail: Albert Ball (#469), Watson Fothergill (#467), Jane Fraser (#471), Samuel Waite Johnson (#24), Herbert Durrant Snook (#351), Marriott Ogle Tarbotton (#201). Uploads survive a deploy now.

tasks.title: Put Dougal de Havilland's map in the archive
tasks.detail: The PDF itself, with credit, so the record holds the source and not only what was mined from it.

tasks.title: The 1911 birth places
tasks.detail: 330 of 902 people in the 1911 census have a birth place against 1,272 of 1,289 for 1921. This is the hole in the origins map.

tasks.title: Work the forename sex queue down
tasks.detail: Setting a name once covers everyone who shares it, so this goes faster than it looks.

tasks.title: Confirm or throw out the Wikidata suggestions
Confirm or throw out the Gazette notices
tasks.detail: The links now go to the notice page rather than the PDF. Tell me if they still give a 403 from America.

tasks.title: Add the null DKIM record
tasks.detail: TXT at *._domainkey with v=DKIM1; p= — says no DKIM signature is valid for the domain and clears the last of Cloudflare's recommendation.

tasks.title: Pick one canonical host and redirect the other
tasks.detail: www or the apex, 301 in Cloudflare's redirect rules. Sessions are per hostname, so signing in on one leaves you signed out on the other.

tasks.title: Check Cloudflare's SSL mode says Full (strict)
tasks.detail: It is already Full or it would be looping. Strict validates the origin certificate and costs nothing.

tasks.title: Restrict the Google Maps key to the new domain
tasks.detail: The key is handed to every visitor's browser. Add nottinghamparkhouses.com and www, and keep the Railway address until everything has moved.

tasks.title: Decide whether /join should carry an email address
tasks.detail: It says an administrator approves accounts. If you would rather people wrote to you first, that needs an address on it.

tasks.title: Find which building on Derby Road was the Bayley Hospital
tasks.detail: An auxiliary hospital from October 1914 under Lilian Birkin, among the first three in England to take military patients and more than 1,600 casualties in four years. Derby Road is this record's northern edge and it holds 117 to 173 and Rocky Mount. If the building is one of ours it is the most significant wartime use in the record.

tasks.title: Run Import people for the 1901 Lenton Avenue households
tasks.detail: Twenty-three records at 2, 4, 6 and 8 Lenton Avenue: the Thompsons, the Blythes with a boarder, the Sims with a boarder, and the Elmores with a boarder. Fourteen new people; the Blythes and the Sims join their existing 1911 records. The preview should say 14 would be added, 9 already present and 23 census records.

tasks.title: Check Parker Woodward's 1901 record at 25 Cavendish Crescent South
tasks.detail: Entry 562 files him at #49 in 1901 with no relationship and no age, but he is not on the Jessop schedule — the page runs Zebedee Jessop, his four children and three servants, and ends. Probably misfiled from another address.

tasks.title: Run Import people for Harry Judah Weinberg of 4 North Road
tasks.detail: From the 1929 Gazette notice of his estate. One new person, linked to the new property 4 North Road (#412), with his date of death, his occupation and the notice written into his story. The preview should say 1 would be added, 1 property link, 1 occupation.

tasks.title: Place 4 North Road by hand
tasks.detail: Created from the Weinberg Gazette notice and put provisionally between 2 North Road (the Walton Hotel) and 8. OpenStreetMap has no 4 at all, so it may have been absorbed into a neighbour or renumbered.

tasks.title: Don't set aside "SR1 South Rd" — part of it is 3 South Road entered twice
tasks.detail: Four of its seventeen records are the McCraith household already filed at 3 South Road in 1911, imported a second time with the surname spelt McCaith. Douglas McCraith (#186) is in both, so he has two 1911 records — remove entry 889. Then merge by number: keep 185, merge in 728 (Maria Elizabeth); keep 189, merge in 731 (Kenneth York); keep 1343, merge in 732 (Violet Muriel). The other households in the group — Frederick Brewster, and Joseph and Sarah Walker — are not at 3 South Road and still need a house.

tasks.title: Run Import people for the McCraith family
tasks.detail: Bernard McCraith's death on 26 January 1919 as a Major in the Royal Engineers; Lady McCraith's maiden name, Dickinson; and from the report of his will, Sir James's death at Ellenborough House in 1928, his estate, his story and his directorships. Fills blanks only — nothing entered by hand is touched.

tasks.title: Correct Lady McCraith's 1911 relationship — "Head (widow)" should be "Head"
tasks.detail: Settled: Sir James signed the 1911 schedule for Ellenborough House, 3 South Road, but was not there on census night, so Lady McCraith was returned as head and he has no 1911 record. She was not a widow — he lived until 1928. On her page, edit the 1911 census record (entry 271) and change the relationship to Head. His story says why when the McCraith import runs.

tasks.title: Is Malcolm McCraith really Sir James's son?
tasks.detail: The record already links Malcolm (#188), a steam engineer born about 1882, as a son of Sir James and Lady McCraith, and he is at 3 South Road with them in 1891 and 1901. But Wikipedia names their children as Douglas, Bernard, Kenneth York and Violet Muriel only. Either the article misses him or he is a nephew, and the link wants checking.

tasks.title: Run Import people for Sir James McCraith's 1921 household
tasks.detail: Eleven people on Clumber Crescent South, none with a 1921 record before: Sir James, Lady McCraith, Kenneth York and Violet Muriel, their old nurse Isabella Richardson, two visitors and four servants. Ten are already in the record and are joined by number; only the visitor Catherine Wood is new. They arrive unplaced under "Clumber Crescent South". The preview should say 1 would be added, 10 already present, 11 census records.

tasks.title: Which house on Clumber Crescent South were the McCraiths in, in 1921?
tasks.detail: Sir James McCraith's household of eleven is on Clumber Crescent South in 1921 but the number is not known. Every property on the crescent — 3, 5, 7, 9 (Gwedon) and Clumber Court — is empty in 1921, so all five are candidates; the Jardines held 9 in 1911. It was not permanent: the report of his will has him back at Ellenborough House, 3 South Road, when he died in July 1928.

tasks.title: Merge Isabella / Isabelle Richardson, the McCraiths' nurse
tasks.detail: One woman, born in Ireland about 1854, with the McCraiths at 3 South Road from 1891 and on Clumber Crescent South in 1921. Held twice — Isabella (#193) for 1891 and 1901, Isabelle (#733) for 1911. Keep 193, merge in 733.

tasks.title: 3 South Road in 1911 now holds the Brewster household too
tasks.detail: Frederick Brewster, 77, and his three servants were filed to 3 South Road along with the McCraiths, so the house has two heads that year. Brewster's schedule came in the same run but was a household of its own; worth checking it belongs there.

tasks.title: File the Maccoll household to Tower House, 53 Park Row
tasks.detail: Tower House (#395) was already in the record but had no position, so it never appeared on the map. It is now placed from OpenStreetMap and marked Grade II. On /unfiled, the group "tower house park row Park Row" holds Peter Morrison Maccoll, his wife, daughter and a servant — send that household to 395 (the Stubbing household in the same group goes to East Lodge, #413). On the property's Historic England panel, "This is the one" on TOWER HOUSE links its list entry.

tasks.title: (Settled) John Stubbing's return says Park Lodge; the building is East Lodge
tasks.detail: Settled: the lodge is East Lodge on Historic England's list (1270628) and on OpenStreetMap, and Park Lodge is the name the 1921 census gave it. Both names are now on #413. Tick this off.

tasks.title: Merge Louisa Pacey / Paecy, the Sprays' servant for twenty years
tasks.detail: Both born 1872. Louisa Pacey (#2432) is the Spray household's servant at 14 Cavendish Crescent North in 1901; Louisa Paecy (#2101) is still with them at Greendale in 1921. Keep 2432, merge in 2101.

tasks.title: Merge Sissie and Jessie Spray
tasks.detail: Both born 1874, both the Sprays' daughter: "Sissie" (#2431) at 14 Cavendish Crescent North in 1901, Jessie (#2100) at Greendale in 1921. Sissie is a pet name for Jessie. Keep 2100, merge in 2431.

tasks.title: File John Stubbing and Elizabeth Gunn to East Lodge, Park Row
tasks.detail: Their 1921 return reads Park Lodge, Park Row. The building is East Lodge: Historic England's entry 1270628 stands three metres from it and OpenStreetMap names it the same, so it is in the record as East Lodge, Park Row (#413), with Park Lodge kept as the name the census gave it. On /unfiled, in the group "tower house park row Park Row", send the Stubbing household to 413 and the Maccolls to 395.

tasks.title: Work through the house names from Land Registry
tasks.detail: A sweep of HM Land Registry's price paid data across all 44 streets found 797 addresses with a name. Three attached to houses already in the record and are now recorded: Arundel Lodge (1 Park Valley), Castle House (13 Pelham Crescent), and Hardwick House as a second spelling of Hardwicke House. The rest are on /research as nine questions, grouped by street. Belwood is on Tattershall Drive.

tasks.title: Run Import people for Richard Leslie Birkin at Edale House
tasks.detail: A brother of Charles Wilfred Birkin of Newcastle Court, living at Edale House, Clumber Road East in 1911 — from the family account, not a census return, so he is linked to the house as a resident rather than given a census entry. The preview should say 1 would be added, 1 property link, 1 relationship.

tasks.title: Run Import people for the Boot households at St Hellier, 1911 and 1921
tasks.detail: Two files, and the order matters: people_1911_st_hellier.json first, then people_1921_st_hellier.json. The 1911 file creates all thirteen — Sir Jesse Boot, his wife Florence, their three grown children, a visiting barrister from Jersey and seven servants — and files every entry at #402. The 1921 file matches the three Boots by name and adds eight more: John Campbell Boot is head by then, with his parents as visitors. Both run from Import people; preview each first.

tasks.title: Run Import people for Ada Churley of Broadgate School
tasks.detail: Fills her story and gives her occupation its full form — the 1921 return breaks off at "Principal Of Schoo". She is already in the record at 1 Western Terrace, so the preview should say nothing added, 1 filled out, 1 occupation. Her forename stays "A Marion" as the census has it; if you want "Ada" on the record, change it on her person page.

tasks.title: Decide whether Lincoln Circus 3 is Lincoln House, and file the Birkins
tasks.detail: On /unfiled, the group "Lincoln Circus 3" holds Harry Laurence Birkin, his wife Olive and six servants — eight records, 1921. The Birkin family account puts Major Harry Birkin at Lincoln House, Lincoln Circus (#403), which stands empty in the record. If you are satisfied that is the same house, file the household to 403; the identification rests on the account, not on the return, which gives only a number.

tasks.title: Check the two Lincoln Circus 2 records against the Palmers at Gladstone House
tasks.detail: Edward and Alice Palmer appear unfiled under "Lincoln Circus 2" for 1921, and both are already filed at Gladstone House for 1921. Almost certainly the same two records twice. Compare them on /duplicates or on their person pages, then remove whichever copy is the stray — and note that this makes Lincoln Circus 2 the census's name for Gladstone House.

tasks.title: Run Import people for the Fishers of 1 Duke William Mount
tasks.detail: The family the house was built for, from the family account: Horace Arthur Fisher, Sarah Kate née Thackeray, and their six children. The house holds nobody at all in the record, so these are its first people. The preview should say 8 added, 8 property links, 1 marriage and twelve parent links. No census entries are created — there is no return behind this.
